meta.title: Our story
meta.description: Why a restaurant follows the shade: the courtyard houses of Jeddah and Najd, cooking by the hour, and where our ingredients come from.

story.title: Shade before coffee
story.intro: In a hot country, the first thing a host offers is shade. Zill began with that courtesy, and built a kitchen around the way shade moves through a day.

courtesy.title: The first courtesy
courtesy.body: Before coffee, before dates, a host in this land would move you out of the sun. The old houses of Jeddah and Najd were built around a courtyard for that reason: there was always a wall in shade, and the day moved from one wall to the next. Bread was baked by the east wall in the morning, lunch was eaten under the vine, the afternoon was spent in the deepest room, and at night the whole courtyard opened to the sky.

houses.title: Two houses, two suns
houses.body: Lamees Qutub opened the first Zill in a coral-stone house in Al-Balad, Jeddah’s old port town, with a menu written by hand for each part of the day. The second house followed on the edge of the palm groves of Wadi Hanifah in Riyadh: a mud-brick courtyard built from the valley it stands in. Both keep Riyadh time, but not the same sun. Jeddah’s sunset comes some twenty minutes later, and Jeddah, south of the Tropic of Cancer, loses its noon shadow altogether twice a year.

hours.title: Cooking by the hour
hours.body: Our menus follow the light, not the clock on the wall. Morning shade is bread from the tannour, foul and eggs. The short shade is a long lunch to share. The long shade is coffee and something sweet. The night courtyard is the ember grill and the sea. On four evenings a week, the Sundial tells the whole day in seven courses.

sources.title: Where it comes from
sources.body: Dates from Unaizah, honey from Al-Baha, ghee from Al-Kharj, wheat from Hail, coffee from the terraces of Jazan, and fish from the Jeddah market before seven. When something leaves its season, it leaves the menu. When it comes back, so does the dish.

keep.title: What we keep to
keep.body: The beverage programme is alcohol-free. We cook what the hour asks for and little more, so very little is wasted, and what remains becomes the staff lunch. Every menu is written in Arabic first.
